headline: Draft Recap: Lee's Team Builds Around Bijan
summary: A round-by-round look at how Lee's Team came together — from cornerstone Bijan Robinson to a trio of high-upside sleepers.
body:
The board broke our way, and Lee's Team walked away with a roster built to compete right now. Here's a round-by-round look at how it all came together.

HEADLINERS

Round 1, Pick 2 — Bijan Robinson (RB, Atlanta): The cornerstone. Robinson is the consensus RB1A/B heading into 2026 after a monster campaign in which he led the entire NFL with 2,298 scrimmage yards — 1,478 on the ground and 820 more through the air on 79 catches. With the old coaching staff and Tyler Allgeier gone, his goal-line workload should only grow, and a league-best 30% missed-tackle rate makes him a true every-week difference-maker. Landing him at 1.02 hands this roster its foundation.

Round 2, Pick 9 — Rashee Rice (WR, Kansas City): High risk, high reward. When healthy, Rice looked like a star, averaging 18.8 PPR points per game across eight games in 2025. Despite his offseason knee surgery, Rice is expected to be ready for training camp, and in Kansas City's offense he carries genuine top-five receiver upside. There's injury and off-field risk here, but that ceiling in the second round is a swing worth taking.

Round 3, Pick 2 — Brock Bowers (TE, Las Vegas): A steal at 3.02. Bowers is already one of the very best tight ends in football — in a tier of his own alongside Trey McBride — and he commands a massive target share with little competition for looks in Vegas. Projections peg him near 995 yards and seven touchdowns, and an elite tight end is a weekly matchup nightmare most of the league simply can't answer. Grabbing that positional edge in the third round is how you win a draft.

UNDER CENTER

Round 7, Pick 2 — Jayden Daniels (QB, Washington): The engine. Daniels is a consensus top-five fantasy quarterback thanks to elite rushing ability that gives him one of the highest weekly floors at the position. His 2025 was derailed by a run of injuries, but a healthy season makes him a legitimate QB1 — and getting that upside all the way in Round 7 is tremendous value. If he stays on the field, this is a league-winning price for a starter.

SLEEPERS

Round 6, Pick 9 — Jadarian Price (RB, Seattle): A rookie flier with real juice. Seattle spent a first-round pick (No. 32 overall) on Price out of Notre Dame, where he racked up 1,692 rushing yards and 21 touchdowns despite never starting a single game. At 5-10, 203 with excellent vision and balance, he has the tools to earn a role quickly with the Seahawks backfield opened up. A perfect sixth-round pick with upside.

Round 10, Pick 9 — Jaylen Warren (RB, Pittsburgh): A high-floor late-round back. Warren set career highs in 2025 with 211 carries, 958 yards and eight touchdowns, finishing as a top-20 fantasy RB while ranking among the league's best in yards after contact. His outlook is murkier in 2026 with a new coaching staff and the arrival of Rico Dowdle, but he profiles as a strong pass-catcher who should still have a large role in this Steelers offense. As a Round 10 bench piece, the value outweighs the risk.

Round 12, Pick 9 — Chris Godwin (WR, Tampa Bay): A classic late-round dart throw. The veteran slot man is working back from the ankle injury that wrecked 2024 and a fibula issue that shortened 2025, but reports had him a standout in offseason work with no lingering concerns. If healthy, Godwin should still offer dependable PPR utility even if his ceiling isn't what it once was. At 12.09, there's essentially no downside — pure upside insurance.

Now the work begins. Season 1 kicks off September 9th — let's make this the year we finally break through.

headline: Buzz: Lee's Team Interested In Bijan Robinson at No. 2
summary: Word out of the war room is that Lee's Team has its sights set on Falcons superstar Bijan Robinson — and there's a growing belief that he could slide right to the second pick.
body:
Connect the dots and the target comes into focus: Lee's Team wants Bijan Robinson.

The Falcons' 24-year-old workhorse is coming off a monster season, leading the entire NFL with 2,298 scrimmage yards while scoring 11 touchdowns and hauling in 79 catches for 820 yards on 103 targets. That is genuine three-down, every-week RB1 production, and it is exactly why he enters 2026 as a candidate for the No. 1 overall fantasy pick.

The situation only strengthens the case. Atlanta let change-of-pace back Tyler Allgeier walk this offseason, and although veteran Brian Robinson Jr. was brought in on a modest one-year deal to spell him, this backfield unmistakably belongs to Bijan. New head coach Kevin Stefanski — a two-time AP Coach of the Year — has a long history of leaning on his lead back with a heavy workload and the goal-line role, which could push Robinson's touchdown ceiling even higher than last year's total.

So why the confidence that he falls to No. 2? Chatter around the league suggests the team on the clock at No. 1 may be leaning toward selecting a different player. If that holds, Robinson slides a single spot, and Lee's Team is reportedly ready to sprint to the podium with the card already filled out.

Nothing is official until the pick is turned in. But if the board breaks the way reports suggest, Bijan Robinson won't be falling to pick No. 3.

headline: Lee's Team Lands No. 2 Overall Pick in Draft Lottery
summary: The lottery went Lee's Team's way: the franchise secured the No. 2 overall selection for the 2026 draft — and it has no intention of trading it away.
body:
In this year's draft lottery, Lee's Team jumped up to the No. 2 overall pick — its highest selection in years — and the front office has already made one thing clear: this pick is not for sale.

The timing could not be better. After a gut-punch 6-7 finish last season that left the team on the wrong side of the playoff cutline, the No. 2 overall selection is a genuine chance to reset the trajectory. A few plays here and there and last year looks completely different; now there is premium draft capital to close that gap in a single swing.

The mission is stated plainly: end the drought. Lee's Team has not appeared in the postseason since 2023, and the belief inside the building is that whoever comes off the board at No. 2 can be the missing piece that finally pushes this roster over the hump. Trade offers will come — they always do for a top-two pick — but every signal points to Lee's Team standing pat and making the selection itself.

One draft. One pick. A season's worth of hope riding on getting it right.
